newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOOSNAM OPENS UP TWO-STROKE LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOOSNAM OPENS UP TWO-STROKE LEAD.

text.p: Home golfers seized control of the British PGA Championship on Saturday as Ian Woosnam took the lead with Ryder Cup team mates Nick Faldo, David Gilford and Colin Montgomerie in hot pursuit.
The Welshman charged to a two-stroke lead by defying a frisky, swirling wind to shoot a four-under-par 68 for a nine-under total of 135 on the 6,957-yard Wentworth course.

Faldo, the U.S.-based Englishman who has won this title four times though only once at Wentworth, carded a joint day's best of 67 to advance to seven under, level with quiet northern England cattle farmer Gilford, who shot an erratic 70.

Reigning European number one Montgomerie, a Scot, recorded his second successive three-under-par 69, helped by chip-ins for birdies at the 13th and 14th, but was disappointed not to birdie either of the last two par fives.
He was alone in fourth place on six under, one better than the best overseas players, Trinidad's Stephen Ames and Frank Nobilo of New Zealand who compiled rounds of 69 and 71 respectively.
Joint overnight leaders Irishmen Darren Clarke and Eamonn Darcy fell back with rounds of 74 and 75 and are on four under and three under respectively.
South African Ernie Els was level with Clarke after a 71 but Bernhard Langer of Germany fell away with a 75 after his opening 67. He was on two under par.
Spaniard Jose Maria Olazabal shot 71 to stand on one under but his compatriot and Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros withdrew with a bad back before even beginning his second round.
